Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: Lip swelling after consuming a prawn-containing item; swelling began on the left corner of the lip and progressed to the upper lip, increasing in size. Associated sensation of throat tightness and chest/airway discomfort; patient reports feeling short of breath and dizziness.
- Onset and progression: Swelling started around 7:00 PM (just after work) and developed over approximately 30 minutes; symptoms have been worsening.
- Past medical history: Asthma (regular use of salbutamol inhaler); peanut allergy. Prior history of a severe allergic reaction with swelling and breathing difficulty around age 6 after eating curry.
- Medications: Salbutamol inhaler (asthma) – used regularly; antihistamines not documented as current use; no other medications documented.
- Allergies: Peanut allergy (documented).
- Social history: Currently alone at the time of the call; someone has just arrived to stay with her.

Objective:
- Physical/clinical findings documented: Lip swelling present (upper lip, left side) with reported progression. Patient reports throat swelling and dyspnea. No vitals or detailed physical exam findings provided.
- Investigations: None performed or recorded in this transcript.

Assessment & Plan:
1. Suspected anaphylaxis
   - Assessment (diagnostic label): Suspected anaphylactic reaction to prawn-containing exposure.
   - Differential diagnosis: Food-induced allergic reaction with facial angioedema; angioedema without anaphylaxis; non-specific airway discomfort.
   - Investigations planned: Urgent emergency evaluation by ambulance/EMS.
   - Treatment planned: Ambulance to assess and manage emergently; take available antihistamines in the meantime; ensure someone with the patient and contact emergency services (999) if not already done. Follow-up after hospital on potential injections (epinephrine) and ongoing management.

2. Peanut allergy (history of severe allergy)
   - Assessment: Known peanut allergy with history of potential severe reaction during childhood; risk for future reactions.
   - Differential diagnosis: General peanut allergy–related reaction.
   - Investigations planned: None immediate.
   - Treatment planned: Avoidance guidance and post-event management discussion once stabilized.

3. Asthma history
   - Assessment: Asthma history; uses salbutamol inhaler regularly.
   - Differential diagnosis: Acute airway irritation/bronchospasm risk in context of anaphylaxis.
   - Investigations planned: None immediate.
   - Treatment planned: Continue standard asthma management; not further detailed in this encounter.
